title: From Complexity to Capability: What Manufacturers Told Us at IMTS
summary: At IMTS 2026, one message surfaced again and again: Manufacturers are not looking for more technology.
body_markdown:
**By**[Maya Dav’e](https://www.office.com/search?q=Maya+Dav%27e&EntityRepresentationId=2501c87d-4925-8b17-8691-752c728943c2) **, Marketing Specialist, and**[Madison Maglin](https://www.office.com/search?q=Madison+Maglin&EntityRepresentationId=3d757295-5c89-8764-b53e-1f99860f9dad) **, Marketing Communications Specialist**


At IMTS 2026, one message surfaced again and again: Manufacturers are not looking for more technology. They are looking for ways to make technology work more effectively for their business.


Across conversations about[robotics, automation,](https://novanta.com/capabilities/robotics-automation/)[precision manufacturing](https://novanta.com/capabilities/precision-manufacturing/) , and laser processing, customers consistently focused on the same priorities: Increasing productivity, improving flexibility, addressing labor challenges, enhancing safety, and positioning their operations for long-term growth.


The discussions offered valuable insight into how manufacturing priorities continue to evolve.


**Conversations That Started Small and Grew Bigger**


One of the most consistent themes was how quickly discussions expanded beyond individual products.


Customers often arrived with a specific application, challenge, or technology in mind. In one conversation, a manufacturer brought metal samples directly to the booth and immediately began discussing cutting requirements, production goals, and material characteristics.


The discussion quickly shifted from products to the broader manufacturing challenge.


That pattern repeated throughout the week. A conversation might begin with tooling, motion control, laser processing, or automation. Within minutes, it often expanded into a discussion about productivity, throughput, workforce challenges, scalability, and future growth.


Customers were increasingly interested in understanding how multiple technologies could work together to improve an entire process rather than focusing on a single component.


**Manufacturing Wants Practical Automation**


The show also highlighted an important change in how manufacturers approach automation.


Organizations are moving beyond asking whether automation is possible and instead focusing on how automation can be implemented in a way that makes sense for their operation.


Conversations frequently centered on material handling, precision, safety, labor shortages, flexibility, and the challenge of getting more out of existing equipment. Manufacturers wanted solutions that addressed immediate needs while creating a path for future growth.


This shift reflects a broader industry trend toward practical automation, solutions designed around measurable outcomes rather than technology for technology’s sake.


**Why Integration Matters**


Throughout IMTS, live demonstrations helped bring that perspective to life.


By showcasing motion technologies, end-of-arm tooling, sensing capabilities, automation solutions, and precision manufacturing technologies working together, visitors could see how different parts of the manufacturing ecosystem connect.


The demonstrations helped move conversations away from individual products and toward complete applications.


Rather than evaluating standalone technologies, customers wanted to understand how integrated solutions could improve performance, simplify implementation, and support future scalability.


**The Value of Expertise**


The show also reinforced the importance of technical expertise.


Manufacturers are not simply looking for technology providers. They are looking for partners who understand their applications and can help navigate complex challenges.


One example involved attendees exploring ceramic cutting applications. What started as a technical question evolved into a detailed discussion about application requirements, challenges, and potential solutions. The visitors later described it as one of the most valuable conversations they had experienced at the event.


Those interactions reinforced that meaningful customer relationships are built not only through technology, but through[expertise](https://novanta.com/about/) and a deep understanding of customer challenges.


**Simplicity Is Becoming a Competitive Advantage**


Perhaps the strongest takeaway from the week was the growing demand for simplicity.


Manufacturers face increasing pressure to improve performance while managing workforce challenges, operational complexity, and evolving customer expectations. As a result, they are looking for partners who can simplify decision-making and provide a clear path forward.


Customers repeatedly emphasized that they do not need to understand every technology component. They want to understand how a solution will solve a problem and help them achieve their goals.


The most successful conversations at IMTS were not about the complexity of the technology. They were about the[outcomes](https://novanta.com/about/vision-mission/) that technology could deliver.


**Looking Beyond the Technology**


IMTS provided more than a showcase of emerging technologies. It offered a real-time view into the future of manufacturing.


Whether the goal is improving productivity, increasing precision, creating flexibility, overcoming workforce constraints, or preparing for future growth, manufacturers continue to evaluate technology through the lens of outcomes.


If there was one takeaway that connected conversations across the show floor, it was this: manufacturers don’t want more complexity. They want practical solutions, trusted expertise, and partners who can help them move forward with confidence.
